Authors: D. Srivastava, S. Puri, S. D. Bhagat, and M. Verma
Title: Emotify: An AI-Powered Emotion-Based Music Recommendation System
Methodology: CNN-based facial emotion detection connected to a music recommendation layer
Dataset: Facial emotion images and music metadata
Performance/Accuracy: Prototype-level emotion-aware recommendation with practical CNN integration
Salient Features: Direct mapping from detected mood to song suggestions; deployable demo architecture
Limitations: Primarily image-centric and limited in multimodal fusion depth
Summary: Demonstrates that emotion-aware recommendation can be implemented in a lightweight end-to-end academic system.

Authors: A. Chikaraddi, S. G. Janakki, S. G. Kanakaraddi, and P. S. M.
Title: Emotion-Driven Music Recommender System with Deep Learning and Streamlit Integration
Methodology: Deep learning-based emotion detection wrapped in a Streamlit user interface
Dataset: FER-style facial emotion data with curated music recommendations
Performance/Accuracy: Functional real-time pipeline and usable recommendation loop
Salient Features: Combines deep learning inference with modern lightweight app deployment
Limitations: Still centered on a narrow input path and focused mostly on music response
Summary: Shows the feasibility of deployable emotion-aware recommendation using a web interface familiar to Python students.

Authors: M. A. Talaghat, E. Parvinnia, and R. Boostani
Title: Content-based music recommender system based on music emotion using deep learning
Methodology: Deep learning for content-based music emotion understanding
Performance/Accuracy: Improved content-level recommendation relevance over simpler feature pipelines
Salient Features: Useful when user history is weak but content metadata is available
Limitations: Focuses on item emotion rather than a broader lifestyle adaptation framework
Summary: Important for understanding how music-side emotion intelligence complements user-side mood detection.

Authors: B. Pan, K. Hirota, Z. Jia, and Y. Dai
Title: A review of multimodal emotion recognition from datasets, preprocessing, features, and fusion methods
Methodology: Comprehensive survey of preprocessing, feature extraction, and fusion strategies
Dataset: Survey across IEMOCAP, MELD, DEAP and related MER datasets
Performance/Accuracy: Survey paper synthesizing trends rather than a single benchmark
Salient Features: Strong reference for multimodal pipeline design and dataset choices
Limitations: No directly deployable end-to-end system is validated
Summary: Provides conceptual backbone for choosing multiple modalities, fusion strategies, and evaluation criteria.

Authors: X. Zhu, C. Guo, H. Feng, and Y. Huang
Title: A Review of Key Technologies for Emotion Analysis Using Multimodal Information
Methodology: Taxonomy of multimodal emotion analysis technologies and fusion methods
Dataset: Speech, text, image, and physiological datasets
Performance/Accuracy: Survey paper summarizing performance trends and open issues
Salient Features: Highlights missing-modality handling, efficiency, synchronization, and cross-domain transfer
Limitations: Does not directly present a low-resource practical system
Summary: Supports the need for fusion-aware and deployment-aware design in affective computing projects.

Authors: M. P. A. Ramaswamy and S. Palaniswamy
Title: Multimodal emotion recognition: A comprehensive review, trends, and challenges
Methodology: Comprehensive review of multimodal emotion recognition
Performance/Accuracy: Survey-led trend analysis rather than direct experimentation
Salient Features: Emphasizes explainability, lightweight models, and generalization challenges
Limitations: Broad review, so system-building details remain abstract
Summary: Reinforces the need for practical trade-offs between accuracy, transparency, and real-world deployability.

Title: Integrating BERT Embeddings and BiLSTM for Emotion Analysis of Dialogue
Methodology: BERT word and sentence embeddings fused with BiLSTM sequence modeling
Performance/Accuracy: Outperformed baseline dialogue emotion classifiers on evaluated corpora
Salient Features: Captures context-sensitive emotion better than shallow text models
Limitations: Text-only orientation and heavier inference demands than rule-based methods
Summary: Useful for motivating the optional free API upgrade path for richer text emotion understanding.

Title: Self-Learning Multimodal Emotion Recognition Based on Multi-Scale Dilated Attention
Methodology: EEG and facial analysis using multi-scale dilated attention with self-learning fusion
Performance/Accuracy: High reported accuracy on multimodal DEAP and strong facial branch results
Salient Features: Shows the power of adaptive decision-level fusion in emotion recognition
Limitations: Requires modalities and computation that may not fit low-cost student deployment
Summary: A strong advanced benchmark that inspires fusion design while revealing the cost of sophisticated architectures.

Authors: J. Wu, J. Wu, Y. Zheng, P. Zhan, and M. Han
Title: MLGAT: multi-layer graph attention networks for multimodal emotion recognition in conversations
Methodology: Graph attention modeling over text, speech, and image modalities
Dataset: Conversation-centric multimodal corpora such as MELD
Performance/Accuracy: Improved robustness and accuracy over traditional multimodal baselines
Salient Features: Models cross-utterance and cross-modality relationships effectively
Limitations: Less suitable for low-resource single-file deployment
Summary: Important for understanding why relationship-aware multimodal fusion remains a future-scope direction.

Authors: B. Liu, J. Guo, C. L. P. Chen, X. Wu, and T. Zhang
Title: Fine-Grained Interpretability for EEG Emotion Recognition: Concat-Aided Grad-CAM and Systematic Brain Functional Network
Methodology: Grad-CAM-based interpretability with graph learning over brain functional networks
Performance/Accuracy: State-of-the-art subject-dependent performance with improved interpretability
Salient Features: Shows that explainability can be deeply integrated into affective models
Limitations: EEG-centric setup is not straightforward for everyday student use
Summary: Supports the argument that emotion AI must provide interpretable evidence, not only class labels.

Title: Facial emotion recognition: A comprehensive review
Dataset: CK+, FER2013, RAF-DB and related datasets
Performance/Accuracy: Survey of model classes and domain applications
Salient Features: Synthesizes CNN, transfer learning, and in-the-wild recognition challenges
Limitations: Does not directly address recommendation and lifestyle adaptation
Summary: Provides justification for image-based emotion analysis as one modality of the proposed system.

Title: Ethical considerations in emotion recognition technologies: a review of the literature
Methodology: Ethical literature review across emotion recognition technology contexts
Performance/Accuracy: Not a benchmark paper; derives ethical themes and governance guidance
Salient Features: Highlights bias, privacy, data sensitivity, and contextual harm
Limitations: Does not provide a concrete engineering implementation
Summary: Directly motivates the Ethical AI monitor used in the proposed project.

Title: Human Digital Twin in Industry 5.0: A Holistic Approach to Worker Safety and Well-Being through Advanced AI and Emotional Analytics
Methodology: Human digital twin framework integrating safety, well-being, and emotional analytics
Dataset: Conceptual and applied worker analytics context
Performance/Accuracy: Framework-level contribution with strong application significance
Salient Features: Introduces emotional analytics as part of a practical digital twin view of human state
Limitations: Industrial scope differs from student lifestyle support
Summary: Provides the conceptual basis for the project’s Digital Emotional Twin logging idea.

Authors: F. Liu, Q. Cao, X. Huang, and H. Liu
Title: Sentimentally enhanced conversation recommender system
Methodology: Emotion semantics, knowledge graph enhancement, and conversation-aware recommendation
Performance/Accuracy: Strong improvements over baseline CRS approaches in public benchmarks
Salient Features: Shows that emotional semantics can meaningfully improve recommendation quality
Limitations: Conversation-heavy architecture is more complex than needed for a low-resource prototype
Summary: Important evidence that affect-aware recommendation improves relevance beyond static recommendation logic.

Authors: Y. Yang, Z. Wang, L. Li, and D. Zeng
Title: Emotion-Enhanced Dual-Agent Recommendation: Understanding and Leveraging Cognitive Conflicts for Better Personalization
Methodology: Dual-agent recommendation guided by emotion and cognitive conflict modeling
Dataset: Recommendation datasets with affective or cognitive-conflict signals
Salient Features: Connects emotional reasoning and personalization in a richer decision process
Limitations: Heavier recommendation logic and less focused on explainable single-app deployment
Summary: Supports the claim that emotion should influence recommendation ranking, not only classification.

Authors: Y. Li, J. Chan, G. Peko, and D. Sundaram
Title: An explanation framework and method for AI-based text emotion analysis and visualisation
Methodology: Framework for explaining AI-based text emotion analysis and visualization
Performance/Accuracy: Demonstrates practical explanation strategies for emotion analysis outputs
Salient Features: Bridges emotion AI and explanation design in user-facing systems
Limitations: Focuses on text explanation rather than multimodal operational systems
Summary: Useful for motivating why the system should expose evidence, confidence, and reflective reasoning to users.

Authors: A. Shulner-Tal, T. Kuflik, D. Kliger, and A. Mancini
Title: Who Made That Decision and Why? Users’ Perceptions of Human Versus AI Decision-Making and the Power of Explainable-AI
Methodology: User-centered XAI analysis of perceived fairness and comprehensibility
Performance/Accuracy: Shows explanations can reduce trust and fairness gaps between AI and human decisions
Salient Features: Demonstrates the behavioral value of transparent AI interfaces
Limitations: Not an emotion recommendation model itself
Summary: Strengthens the case for embedding explainability and confidence disclosures in the project interface.

Title: How Explainable AI Affects Human Performance: A Systematic Review of the Behavioural Consequences of Saliency Maps
Methodology: Behavioral review of explainability impacts on human performance
Performance/Accuracy: Shows explanation quality influences human trust and task performance
Salient Features: Directly relevant to the use of Grad-CAM and saliency-like visual evidence
Limitations: General XAI scope rather than specific mood recommendation deployment
Summary: Provides supporting evidence that explanation tools improve usability when designed responsibly.
